# USR-007: Root recovery path is known

- **Group:** Users and privilege
- **Severity when it fails:** info
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

Whether root has a password decides your way back in when SSH keys fail: a locked root means provider console or rescue mode only. The status is printed so you know your recovery path before you need it.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo passwd -S root
```

## How to fix it

Store the console or rescue procedure and any root password in a password manager.
